in_arabic.name: إمير
in_arabic.meaning: أمير الرجال، قائد الجيش، سيد الشباب، زعيم المجتمع
in_arabic.long_meaning: الاسم الإسمي إمير هو اسم عربي قديم يعني أمير الرجال و قائد الجيش، و هو من أسماء المؤثرين في المجتمع، حيث كان الأمير يعتبر زعيم المجتمع و سيد الشباب، و كان له دور كبير في توجيههم و حمايةهم، و هو من أسماء الإلهام و الإرادة، و هو اسم يرمز إلى القوة و العزلة، و هو من أسماء النجاح و التألق

in_urdu.name: امیر
in_urdu.meaning: امیر کے معنی ہیں قائد، سربراہ، رہنما، زعیم
in_urdu.long_meaning: امیر نام ہے عربی زبان کا جس کے معنی قائد، سربراہ، رہنما، زعیم کے ہیں، یہ نام مسلمانوں میں بہت مقبول ہے اور اسلامی روایات کے مطابق امیر نام کے صاحبان کو قیادت اور سربراہی کی صلاحیت بہت ہوتی ہے، اس نام کو بچوں کی پیدائش پر دیتے ہیں تاکہ وہ قیادت اور سربراہی کی سکھ لے اور مستقبل میں ایسے شخص بن سکیں جو ایسے ہی ہو جو اپنے ملک اور امت کے لیے قائد بنے

in_hindi.name: अमीर
in_hindi.meaning: अमीर के अर्थ हैं नेता, सर्वेश्वर, प्रशासक, राजा
in_hindi.long_meaning: अमीर नाम है अरबी भाषा का जिसके अर्थ नेता, सर्वेश्वर, प्रशासक, राजा के होते हैं, यह नाम मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत लोकप्रिय है, और इस्लामिक परंपराओं के अनुसार अमीर नाम वालों को नेतृत्व और प्रशासन की क्षमता बहुत अच्छी होती है, इस नाम को बच्चों के जन्म पर दिया जाता है ताकि वे नेतृत्व और प्रशासन की शिक्षा ले सकें और भविष्य में ऐसे व्यक्ति बन सकें जो अपने देश और समुदाय के लिए नेता बन सकें

in_english.name: Emir
in_english.meaning: Emir means a leader, a commander, a chief, a head, a prominent person
in_english.long_meaning: The name Emir is of Arabic origin and means a leader, a commander, a chief, a head, a prominent person. In Islamic tradition, Emir is considered a name that signifies leadership, power, and authority. People with the name Emir are often associated with qualities such as strength, courage, and determination. The name Emir is also commonly found in many Muslim cultures, including Turkish, Urdu, and Pashto-speaking communities. Emir is a popular name among Muslim parents who want their child to grow up to be a leader and a prominent figure in society.

data.cultural_impact: An Emir was a paramount leader in Islamic history, ruling over a specific region or principality. The title symbolized authority, leadership, and military prowess. Emirs contributed significantly to the spread of Islam, as they established and maintained Islamic states, and often sponsored religious institutions, promoting Islamic learning and tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: An Emir, as a ruler, was expected to govern justice, uphold Islamic principles, and protect the community from harm. The spiritual significance of the title "Emir" lies in its association with being a God-designated leader, responsible for providing guidance, ensuring peace and security, and safeguarding the moral and spiritual well-being of the ruled community. An Emir was expected to govern with wisdom, compassion, and piety, with his actions reflecting traditional Islamic values and ethics.

historical_references.reference: Al-Mamun, the Abbasid Caliph, appointed the Turkish general Tahir ibn Husain as Emir of Khorasan in 821. Tahir established the Tahirid Dynasty which ruled over Khorasan and Transoxiana until 873.
historical_references.context: The Tahirid Dynasty was an independent state within the Abbasid Caliphate ruling over Khorasan and Transoxiana, established when the Caliph appointed a Turkish general as Emir to govern these regions.

historical_references.reference: The Umayyad Emir of Seville, Al-Mansur, successfully defended the city from Christian invasion in 712. He later expanded his territory by reconquering parts of the Iberian Peninsula.
historical_references.context: The Umayyad Emirate of Seville was a powerful Muslim state in the Iberian Peninsula, with Al-Mansur being a notable ruler who defended the city against Christian invasion and expanded the territory.
